ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.2 meters. It features a bronze-brown dorsum with distinct black lateral stripes and a pale venter. A prominent black postocular stripe is its primary diagnostic feature.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dendrelaphis caudolineolatus* is best identified by the prominent, continuous black stripe running along the sides of its tail, which is absent in other similar species.
ai.habitat: This species inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Gunther's Bronzeback is a diurnal, arboreal hunter that actively pursues lizards and frogs through the forest canopy with remarkable speed and agility.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis caudolineolatus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: Dendrelaphis caudolineolatus is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka at mid-to-high elevations.
